page: Amazon Web Services r5d.large is a memory-optimized Nitro-based virtual machine instance designed for memory-intensive applications requiring direct-attached NVMe storage. Powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor, it provides 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU configuration features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, supporting instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512F, BMI2, and AES. Hardware acceleration via GPUs is not included.

The instance delivers 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, establishing a high memory allocation of 8.0 GB per core. In addition to general RAM capacity, the hardware incorporates 75 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage. Baseline network performance is rated at 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate modest computational throughput, aligned with its 2-vCPU envelope. Stress-ng single-core performance reached 1276.49 (bottom 25%) and multi-core scored 1678.07 (bottom 10%). Geekbench recorded a single-core score of 1055.0 and a multi-core score of 1247.0, with PassMark measuring an overall CPU score of 2000.63. Memory bandwidth testing indicated 96.24 GB/sec for cached read-only blocks, dropping to 13.57 GB/sec read and 11.56 GB/sec write for uncached 256 MB blocks. In application benchmarks, the instance recorded 1.69 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.03 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the r5d.large lies in its modest raw CPU and bandwidth ceilings against its generous memory-to-vCPU ratio and high-speed local NVMe scratch storage. This profile yields efficient cost resource density for entry-tier relational databases, in-memory caches, staging environments, and intermediate data processing jobs that demand local high-speed disk caching without the expense of broader compute instances.
description: Amazon Web Services r5d.large is a memory-optimized Nitro virtual server powered by a 3.1 GHz Intel Xeon 8259CL processor with 2 vCPUs across 1 physical core. It features 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 75 GB NVMe SSD for fast local instance storage and a 1 Gbps baseline network link. Benchmark results place both compute and memory throughput in the lower percentiles, reflecting its entry-tier 2-vCPU sizing with a PassMark CPU score of 2000.63 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 1247.0. While raw compute performance is limited, the integration of dedicated local SSD storage and a substantial memory footprint makes this instance cost-effective for smaller relational databases, in-memory key-value caching such as Redis, and temporary data staging tasks.
